title.narrative: Multi-sectoral assistance to the most vulnerable internally displaced people in collective sites found in Shire city, Tahtay Adyabo woreda and Adwa

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Tigray regional state in Ethiopia currently hosts over 749,509 internally displaced persons (IDPs) (DTM Ethiopia, 2024). The Northwestern Zone, particularly Shire city, accommodates the largest concentration of IDPs in the region. Specifically, Shire city and Tahtay Adyabo are home to 308,904 and 30,156 IDPs, respectively, with women accounting for approximately half of this population. Additionally, Adwa town in the Central Zone of Tigray also hosts 39,814 IDPs. The IDPs across the target areas reside in collective centers, informal settlements, and host community settings (PAD, 2025). ltbrgtThe humanitarian situation in these areas is worsening due to conflict, protracted displacement, lack of services, reduced humanitarian attention, weather-related shocks, and persistent economic hardships (PAD, 2025). A significant majority of IDPs live in host communities within unfinished buildings, damaged shelters, and open spaces, further exposing them to diseases, theft, and protection risks. The approaching rainy season is expected to worsen the humanitarian situation across the target areas. Vulnerable groups such as women, girls, children, and people with disabilities are disproportionately affected by these multiple crises (PAD, 2025 Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), April 2025). Critical gaps remain in terms of Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), with severe shortages in shelter, food, water, sanitation, hygiene (WASH) services, medical care, and other essential infrastructure. These deficiencies significantly heighten the risk of communicable disease outbreaks and other protection concerns across the target areas (PAD, 2025). Currently, only about 30% of IDPs residing in Shire city and the surrounding woredas are receiving assistance, underscoring the urgent need for ES/NFI and CCCM interventions.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe primary objective of the proposed project is to deliver multi-sectoral assistance to the most vulnerable IDPs residing in collective sites and with the host community in Shire city, Tahtay Adyabo Woreda, and Adwa town. For achieving this objective, PAD will partner with sub-national and national clusters, relevant government offices, community representatives, and CSOs operating at the local levels. Addressing the challenges IDPs are facing across the target areas requires sustained support and collaboration among humanitarian actors, government authorities, and the international community. For this purpose, various strategies such as community engagement, capacity building, behavioral change communication, and partnership will be utilized. PAD will utilize supportive supervision for following up on the progress of the project.ltbrgt ltbrgtIn recognition of the above challenges, PAD has designed interventions that focus on ES/NFI interventions in Shire City and Tahtay Adyabo Woreda while CCCM interventions will be implemented in Tahtay Adyabo and Adwa town. Following the needs assessment conducted by PAD and prioritization of the sub-national cluster, a total of 12 sites will be targeted in this project. In this project, PAD will target a total of 36,259 individuals, including 20,723 women. Of these, 19,294 individuals are targeted for ES-NFI assistance, while 16,965 are targeted for CCCM interventions. Additionally, 4,363 persons with disabilities will be included in the target population (2,485 are women). The project will be implemented from July 01, 2025, to March 31, 2026, with a total budget of $850,000. It aligns with the objectives of the national CCCM cluster and ES/NFI cluster, contributing to strategic objectives 1, 3, 4, and 5 of the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) 2025. Furthermore, it corresponds with the priority areas and response modalities established by the sub-national clusters for both CCCM and ES/NFI sectors.ltbrgtlt/pgt
